exposure: Contracting out of primary and secondary healthcare facilities
outcome: Service volumes (general outpatient department, consultancy services, emergency services, facility-based deliveries, antenatal care visits, immunisation volumes)
Availability of drugs, equipment, supplies, water and electricity
cohort: The study utilized secondary data from district health information systems and included health managers and patients in Thatta and Sujawal districts of Sindh province, Pakistan.
finding: Contracting out of primary and secondary healthcare facilities led to improved service volumes across several indicators, though challenges with autonomy and drug availability persisted.
mod_finding: Facility-based deliveries increased by 37% following the contracting out initiative.
